title: Principal Investigator, Quarter-Hour Boundary Lab
verdict_why: Only 3 lab notes on record (need >= 50) — not enough history for any scientific verdict. I keep watching the clock.
verdict_plain: Clara's verdict: hold and keep watching. The boundary evidence so far is neither strong enough to apply nor weak enough to withdraw — the watch stays open, ticking.
model_gates: APPLY_CANDIDATE nominates only. Adoption requires the runner's champion/challenger gates: held-out Brier improvement ≥ 2e-4, positive in both halves, family-wise α=0.05 with Bonferroni correction, ≥24h between adoptions. WITHDRAW recommends boundaryWeight 0. This file never changes a weight directly.

hypotheses.claim: Returns at quarter-hour boundary openings (:00/:15/:30/:45) carry predictable structure that off-grid bars do not.
hypotheses.prediction: boundary-issued reads align with subsequent direction more often than chance

hypotheses.claim: The quarter-hour member beats the baseline forecast out-of-sample on Brier score.
hypotheses.prediction: member Brier < baseline Brier over n ≥ 200 scored forecasts

hypotheses.claim: Volume bursts at boundary bars mark periodic algorithmic flow, and bursts condition the effect: loud boundary bars predict better than quiet ones.
hypotheses.prediction: average burst ratio above the off-grid norm in decisive cycles

hypotheses.claim: The boundary effect expresses itself often enough to matter — not a once-a-quarter curiosity.
hypotheses.prediction: decisive_frac ≥ 0.40 over rolling history once n ≥ 100

disciplines_applied.assessment: boundary volume runs 2.29x the off-grid norm on average; decisive 66.7% of cycles. Periodicity is an estimate against a noisy tape, not a fact — hours of grid history are what keep it honest.
No edge to explain — and I will not pretend a quiet boundary bar was ever a signal.

A boundary is a definition before it is a discovery: bars opening at minute 0, 15, 30, 45 of the hour. Change the grid definition and the effect must be re-measured — phase is part of the result, and placebo phases are the control.
When in doubt I vote HOLD: adopting noise corrupts every forecast it touches, and that is the costliest error I can make.
Instrument flag: bar data blind 33.3% of cycles — a feed gap at a boundary bar masquerades as a quiet grid unless you check liveness, and I check.

Everyone can see the clock — that is precisely the problem. If boundary flow were a free lunch, the crowd standing at :00/:15/:30/:45 would have eaten it. The edge, if any, is in conditioning on the burst and the agreement, not in "the quarter-hour moved." That is why no APPLY verdict of mine ever skips out-of-sample proof.
Known: decisive 66.7% of cycles, mean sign persistence 75.0%. Unknown: whether the phase structure survives the next change in who trades this market and when. Confidence: low — the honest answer.
Hypothesis ledger updated — statuses changed only where the evidence moved them; nothing was buried and nothing was accepted without a test.
I sign this verdict: HOLD. It is defensible from the record below, and I will reverse it the moment the evidence does.
